Sui: mainnet 3 May 2023 via Binance Launchpool (33rd project), day-1 spot listing, opened ~$1.33 vs 3c presale / 10c public sale — VC + market-maker backed from second zero.
Aptos: $200M Series A (Jump Crypto et al) July 2022 + Binance Labs strategic investment; genesis 12 Oct 2022, mainnet 18 Oct 2022 with day-1 Binance AND Coinbase listings.
Celestia (TIA): airdrop claim window 26 Sep–17 Oct 2023, 60M TIA (6% of supply) to 576,653+ addresses; mainnet + exchange listings 31 Oct 2023.

Berachain (BERA): mainnet + Binance day-1 listing 6 Feb 2025 13:00 UTC (BTC/USDT/USDC/BNB/FDUSD/TRY pairs), $600M+ airdrop, ATH $14.83 (~$1.17B) then -96% by mid-Dec — shows a bought day-1 listing does NOT create durable value.

Market-maker economics: retainer model ~$2k-15k/month (~$10k typical), you keep token custody; loan/call-option model = MM borrows 1-5% of supply for 1-2 years compensated via call options, no upfront cash but you cede float and it's the model repeatedly tied to pump-and-dump (Wintermute accusations, Presto/altsignals coverage).

CEX listing fee reality (2024-26): MEXC $50-100k, Gate similar, KuCoin $150-200k, Bybit $150-250k, OKX $300-500k, Binance $300-800k+ — plus $15-60k liquidity/MM on top; Binance now requires public MM disclosure before listing.

Bridge-hack toll (the risk you take on the moment you build external liquidity — nearly every mega-theft is a bridge, and specifically federated-multisig ones): Wormhole ~$326M (120k wETH) 2 Feb 2022; Ronin ~$625M (173,600 ETH + 25.5M USDC) 23 Mar 2022, a 5-of-9 validator multisig with 5 keys stolen by Lazarus; Harmony Horizon $100M June 2022, a 2-of-5 multisig key compromise; Nomad $190M Aug 2022; Multichain ~$125-130M July 2023 then total collapse after the CEO (sole key-holder) was detained in China. Over $2B stolen from bridges in 2021-22 alone.

BTC-in options and their trust models: WBTC = federated custody (BitGo + BiT Global cold-storage multisig, permissioned merchants) — custodial honeypot; tBTC = Threshold Network node operators, permissionless threshold-sig, no single custodian; THORChain = native BTC settled on both sides, no wrapper and no pooled bridge custody — eliminates the lock-and-mint honeypot entirely.
research.takeaways_for_aincore:
STRUCTURALLY, AINCORE IS KASPA, NOT SUI. With 0% dev-fund, no VC, and no premine, the Sui/Aptos/Berachain 'mainnet + day-1 Binance' path is closed to you — it requires a token allocation to hand the exchange/MM and $300-800k you don't have. Accept the slow bottom-up fair-launch climb; that's a feature (credibility), but plan for it taking 1-2+ years and possibly never reaching tier-1 SPOT (Kaspa hit ~$5B mcap and still can't get Binance/Coinbase spot — futures-only is the realistic ceiling for years).

THE BRIDGE IS NOT OPTIONAL — IT'S THE PRECONDITION FOR ALL LIQUIDITY. Your dex.move AMM is a closed loop: AIN can only be priced against AIN until an external asset (BTC or USDT) physically arrives on-chain. That's the whole point of the bridge. So the sequence is forced: (1) stable mainnet + explorer + wallet, (2) get BTC or USDT on-chain via the SAFEST possible design, (3) seed the ~5M AIN float into an AIN/USDT or AIN/BTC pool, (4) community-crowdfund a small-CEX listing, (5) grow real volume 12-24 months, (6) only then a retainer MM + mid-tier CEX, (7) tier-1 is earned, maybe never.

THE BRIDGE IS ALSO YOUR SINGLE BIGGEST RISK — AND YOUR DESIGN IS THE EXACT FAILURE MODE. Your depin/btc-bridge is federated-multisig with mint DISABLED. Every catastrophic bridge theft was a federated-multisig custody bridge: Ronin (5-of-9, $625M), Harmony (2-of-5, $100M), Multichain (single operator, ~$125M + collapse). A 2-of-3 or 5-of-9 you run means YOU become the custodial honeypot holding everyone's BTC — the most-attacked structure in crypto. Recommendations: keep mint DISABLED until independently audited; strongly prefer NOT running your own custody — route BTC via THORChain-style native settlement (no wrapper, no pooled honeypot) and get USDT via a canonical/native-mint design rather than lock-and-mint pooled custody. If you must run federated custody, that is a mainnet-blocking audit item, not a skeleton to flip on.

MARKET MAKERS: skip until you have a CEX orderbook to make on. When you do, use the RETAINER model (~$2-10k/mo, you keep your tokens) — NOT the loan/call-option model, which hands a chunk of your float to a desk incentivized to pump-and-dump (the Wintermute-accusation pattern). With no treasury you likely can't afford even retainer at first — substitute a community/DAO-funded LP program on your own DEX (fair-launch-native, and how Kaspa did it).

BUDGET HONESTY: steps 1-4 are cheap if you crowdfund the way Kaspa did — the TxBit listing that started KAS's whole journey cost $2,100 of community money. Small-CEX (MEXC/Gate) is $50-100k all-in if you pay yourself; a TxBit/BitMart-tier entry can be low-thousands crowdfunded. The real cost and real danger is not the listing fee — it's the bridge audit. Spend your scarce capital there, not on a vanity listing.

WHAT WON'T WORK: seeding a $10-50k self-DEX pool and calling it a 'price' — it's trivially manipulated and no unknown chain has organic buyers on day one. Liquidity follows real users and real volume; there is no shortcut that substitutes a paid listing or an MM for actual demand. Kaspa's billions came from years of organic community + PoW narrative, not from a launch tactic."

synthesis.how_it_really_works_plain: Nothing actually "moves" between chains. When you "bridge" BTC, the real Bitcoin does not go anywhere — it gets locked with some party (one company, or a group), and a synthetic IOU token representing it is minted on the other chain. That IOU is what trades in an AMM pool. To get your BTC back, the IOU is burned and the locking party releases the real BTC. Bitcoin has no smart contracts and cannot read another chain's state, so SOME off-chain party MUST watch the other chain and sign the Bitcoin release. That party is either ONE entity (custodial: wBTC/BitGo, cbBTC/Coinbase) or a THRESHOLD group (federated: Liquid 11-of-15, RSK, tBTC 51-of-100). There is NO trustless two-way BTC peg in production anywhere — anyone claiming "trustless wrapped BTC" is selling honest-majority or optimistic assumptions with better marketing. Stablecoins are the same story: USDT/USDC only "exist natively" on a chain because Tether/Circle themselves deployed a contract there and hold the real dollars in a bank — they do NOT do this for tiny new chains, and there is no self-serve. Every other USDT/USDC on a small chain is a bridged IOU carrying the exact same custody risk as a BTC bridge, plus a peg you don't control. Your on-chain AMM (dex.move) is the easy 10% — it treats wrapped BTC or a bridged stable as just another token. The hard, dangerous 90% is the off-chain custody in depin/btc-bridge. The entire history of bridge disasters (Ronin $625M, Wormhole $325M, Nomad $190M, Harmony $100M) is the history of that trusted signer set getting compromised, and renBTC ($1B+ TVL) DIED in Dec 2022 with zero hack — its single funder (Alameda) went bankrupt and the bridge held far more BTC than its node bonds secured.
synthesis.realistic_path_for_aincore: Do NOT launch with BTC. Launch AIN against a quote asset you can actually source and control, prove the chain and DEX work with real trading, THEN add a hard-capped federated BTC peg as a later, deliberate milestone — never for a demo. Concretely: (1) Genesis + fair-launch AIN emission live; validators earn AIN. (2) Seed dex.move with your ~5M AIN float paired against a quote asset — realistically your OWN over-collateralized on-chain stablecoin (minted against AIN or against a small custodied BTC reserve you control), because you cannot get native USDT/USDC and a bridged stable is just another custody bridge you'd have to build first anyway. (3) Let the AIN/quote pool run, generate real price discovery and volume, publish it. (4) ONLY THEN build the BTC peg: harden depin/btc-bridge from naive multisig into a threshold-signature scheme (FROST/Taproot-Schnorr or GG20 ECDSA — you already have MPC, threshold-BLS, and multi_sig primitives in common/crypto), with a small set of NAMED, legally-identifiable signers (not anonymous validators), an on-chain HARD CAP on total pegged BTC enforced in the mint path (start at a few BTC, not open-ended), a single public Bitcoin custody address for proof-of-reserves, rate-limits + timelock + a pause/guardian on withdrawals, and an external review before flipping mint_wbtc from DISABLED to enabled. Keeping mint_wbtc DISABLED until all of that exists is the correct current state — do not enable it early. This is not a compromise: a hard-capped, threshold-signed, named-signer federated peg with public reserves IS what Liquid and RSK actually are, and it is the only realistic two-way BTC bridge for a small fair-launch L1.
synthesis.btc_bridge_recommendation: Build a FEDERATED / THRESHOLD-SIGNATURE peg — exactly the depin/btc-bridge federated-multisig skeleton you already have, but hardened. This is honest and correct; it is architecturally identical to Liquid Network (Blockstream, ~11-of-15 functionaries, live since Oct 2018) and RSK Powpeg. You CANNOT realistically be trust-minimized like tBTC v2 (needs a large independent staked signer set + a slashing token you don't have) or BitVM2 (bleeding-edge, week-long dispute windows, huge unaudited pre-signed-transaction engineering — not safe for a small team in 2026). HONEST TRUST STATEMENT to put in your own docs: 'A threshold of named signers holds the locked BTC; if a super-majority of them collude or are legally compelled or have their keys stolen, pegged BTC can be lost. This is not trustless. It is honest-majority custody by identifiable parties, hard-capped so losses are bounded.' Non-negotiable controls, each drawn from a real failure: (a) THE renBTC LAW — pegged BTC value must NEVER exceed the economic security/accountability behind the signers; enforce a hard cap on-chain in the mint path; renBTC held >$1B on ~$100k-per-node bonds and died. (b) Threshold-sig so BTC lives at ONE Bitcoin address and the signer set isn't exposed; plain N-of-N on-chain multisig is the weakest option and is exactly what got Ronin ($625M) and Harmony ($100M) drained. (c) NAMED signers with legal identity — Liquid/RSK work because functionaries are real companies you can sue; anonymous validators mean zero recovery. (d) Public proof-of-reserves address (cbBTC got publicly attacked for lacking an audit). (e) Rate-limit + timelock + pause guardian so one key compromise can't drain in a single block. (f) Treat custody-key GOVERNANCE as a liveness risk, not just theft risk — the Aug 2024 wBTC/BitGo+Justin Sun saga killed wBTC liquidity (Coinbase delisted it, effective Dec 19 2024) with ZERO code failure, purely over WHO got a key; decide and disclose signer governance up front and don't change membership casually. If your real goal is BTC-backed SECURITY rather than tradeable BTC liquidity, look at Babylon's self-custodial BTC staking (~56,000 BTC staked at peak, no bridge honeypot) — but note it does NOT give you BTC you can put in an AMM pool; it solves a different problem.
synthesis.stablecoin_recommendation: There is no free 'just add USDT.' Native USDT/USDC exists on a chain only because Tether/Circle themselves deployed there and hold the real dollars — they evaluate by adoption (supply, holders, apps) and will NOT deploy on a tiny Move-VM L1 on request. Circle's CCTP (the clean burn-and-mint of native USDC) was EVM-only until Solana in Oct 2025 and requires Circle to build contracts FOR your chain — you cannot self-serve it and you're nowhere near the queue. So your only two REAL options, and both must obey the same caps discipline as the BTC bridge: OPTION A (recommended for launch) — your OWN over-collateralized on-chain stablecoin, minted against AIN (and/or against your small custodied BTC reserve), fully on-chain, no external custody bridge, peg maintained by collateral ratio and liquidations. You control it, it needs no third party, and it's the truest fit for fair-launch ethos. Risk: peg is only as strong as collateral + liquidation design, and thin markets can wobble it. OPTION B — a small federated-bridged stablecoin under the SAME hard-cap + named-signer + proof-of-reserves controls as your BTC bridge; this is identical custody risk PLUS a peg you don't control (USDC itself hit $0.87 in March 2023 during SVB), so it buys you a recognizable ticker at the cost of a second custody honeypot. NEVER ship a naive unbacked IOU 'USDT' — that is a rug waiting to happen and will destroy credibility. Decisive pick: launch on your own over-collateralized stable (Option A) as the AIN quote asset; consider a capped bridged stable only much later if real users demand a mainstream dollar.
sequence: 1. Ship genesis + fair-launch AIN emission; validators earn AIN. No pre-mine, no dev fund — matches the locked fair-launch decision.

2. Build/finish your OWN over-collateralized on-chain stablecoin (collateralized by AIN and/or a small self-controlled BTC reserve) as the launch quote asset — do NOT wait on Tether/Circle, they will never natively deploy for you.

3. Seed dex.move: create the AIN / own-stablecoin pool with the ~5M AIN float and matching stablecoin, enabling real on-chain price discovery. This is the easy part — the AMM is generic and already coded.

4. Run and publish real trading: let the pool generate volume and a public price; verify swap/add_liquidity/create_pool on the live path (not just in tests — confirm the deployed code executes), fix slippage/rounding, harden mempool + executor under real load.

5. Design the BTC peg PROPERLY before any BTC touches it: pick a FROST/Taproot-Schnorr or GG20 threshold scheme, recruit a small set of NAMED, legally-identifiable signers, and spec on-chain hard caps, rate-limits, timelock, pause guardian, and a public proof-of-reserves Bitcoin address.
6. Implement + externally review depin/btc-bridge with those controls. The bridge risk is OFF-CHAIN (btc_client/custody), so the review must focus there, not on dex.move.

7. Enable mint_wbtc ONLY after review passes, with the hard cap set to a few BTC. Mint the wrapped-BTC token; list a wBTC/own-stablecoin (or wBTC/AIN) pool on dex.move — for the DEX it's just another token.

8. Operate small, publish reserves continuously, prove peg-in AND peg-out (two-way redemption) works with real BTC, then raise caps slowly as accountability/security behind the signers grows. Never let pegged value outrun the trust backing it.

9. Only much later, if real demand exists, consider a capped federated-bridged mainstream stablecoin (USDT/USDC) under identical custody controls — or, if the goal shifts to BTC-backed security rather than liquidity, evaluate the Babylon self-custodial staking model instead of a bigger bridge.
synthesis.honest_risks: 1) CUSTODY IS THE WHOLE BALLGAME. Your on-chain AMM being done gives a false sense of completion — the existential risk lives entirely off-chain in depin/btc-bridge custody. Every major bridge loss (Ronin $625M Mar 2022, Wormhole $325M Feb 2022, Nomad $190M Aug 2022, Harmony $100M Jun 2022) was the signer set or verification breaking, not the AMM. 2) THE renBTC DEATH MODE. renBTC never got hacked — it died Dec 2022 because its single funder (Alameda) went bankrupt while it held >$1B on ~$100k-per-node bonds. A bridge is only as alive as the entity paying to run it and only as safe as the value backing the signers; if pegged BTC exceeds your economic security/accountability, you are one bad event from insolvency. 3) GOVERNANCE = LIVENESS RISK. The Aug 2024 wBTC saga (BitGo adding a Justin-Sun-linked party) triggered mass redemptions and a Coinbase delisting with zero code failure — WHO holds a key can kill your liquidity overnight. 4) NAMED-SIGNER accountability is your ONLY real recovery path; if your m-of-n are anonymous, theft recovery is zero. 5) STABLECOIN peg risk is real even for the giants (USDC $0.87 in March 2023); your own over-collateralized stable can de-peg if collateral crashes faster than liquidations clear, especially in thin markets. 6) THIN LIQUIDITY: ~5M AIN float is small; a wrapped-BTC or stable pool with shallow depth means brutal slippage and easy price manipulation — cap position sizes and set expectations. 7) DEPLOYED-PATH risk (your own memory flags this): 'the function looks right' has shipped broken fixes before — verify the bridge and DEX code actually execute on the live runtime path, not just in unit tests. 8) REGULATORY: running custody of others' BTC/USD via named signers can carry money-transmission/custody legal exposure depending on jurisdiction — named signers are accountable, which cuts both ways.
what_to_not_do: Do NOT flip mint_wbtc from DISABLED to enabled for a demo or before threshold-sig + hard caps + proof-of-reserves + rate-limits + external review all exist. Its current DISABLED state is correct.
Do NOT claim or imply 'trustless' / 'decentralized' wrapped BTC. It will be a named-signer federated custody peg; label it honestly or you'll lose all credibility on the first challenge.
Do NOT ship a naive unbacked IOU stablecoin named USDT/USDC. That is an unbacked-peg rug and legally toxic.
Do NOT wait on Tether or Circle to natively deploy on AINCORE — they will not for a tiny new L1; there is no self-serve CCTP either.

Do NOT use plain N-of-N on-chain multisig for BTC custody — it exposes the signer set and is exactly the design that got Ronin and Harmony drained. Use threshold signatures so BTC lives at one address.
Do NOT launch BTC first. Prove the chain, the DEX, and a controllable quote asset with real volume before adding any custody honeypot.
Do NOT let total pegged BTC exceed the economic security / signer accountability behind it — enforce a hard cap on-chain in the mint path and start at a few BTC, not open-ended (the renBTC law).
Do NOT use anonymous validators as custody signers — without legal identity your theft-recovery is zero.
Do NOT launch the peg without rate-limits, a withdrawal timelock, and a pause/guardian; a single key compromise must not be able to drain the pool in one block.
Do NOT change custody-key membership casually once live — treat WHO holds keys as a liveness risk, per the wBTC/BitGo delisting precedent.
Do NOT confuse Babylon-style BTC staking with a liquidity bridge — it secures a chain but produces no tradeable BTC for your AMM.
Do NOT trust that 'the code looks right' — verify the bridge and DEX actually execute on the deployed runtime path before declaring anything done.
